races.name: Try Unibet's New Improved Acca Boosts Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Something Coming
runners_data.note: Hold-up style from the Peter Chapple-Hyam yard; has placed twice at 7f on standard Kempton AW (2/5 sim-going placings) suggesting course-track suitability, but an OR of 69 gives only a narrow class edge and Olivia Tubb is an inexperienced handler who must judge the pace carefully from the rear.

runners_data.name: Bundok
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who steps up in distance from his usual 6f comfort zone — his sole run at 7f produced an 11th at Goodwood — and 82 days off the track adds fitness doubt despite the yard's 1/12 14-day strike rate; nonetheless his uncontested lead is the defining tactical asset of this race.

runners_data.name: Unionville
runners_data.note: Held-up type who has managed just one win in ten career starts and whose recent form (178834) shows him finding 7f on Standard AW difficult; Michael Attwater's yard is only 1/17 in 14 days and the 14-day return is a concern, making him hard to elevate.

runners_data.name: Musical Soldier
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in tremendous current form — wins at 7f on Standard AW repeatedly — who carries 138lbs and the lightest possible handicap claim (7lb claim for Libby Swallow); ran just yesterday (1-day return flagged) which is the sharpest query, but three wins from six and an OR of 61 mean he is well treated if all is well.

runners_data.name: Viviana
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up horse by style, but placed into midfield on the map because the field's abundance of rearward types makes the true last position untenable; Charlie Johnston's yard is firing (4/36) and the 14-day return is fine, but her sole Standard AW placing from seven tries (1/7) makes course-going form a clear red flag.

runners_data.name: Chapman's Peak
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's gelding is a natural hold-up performer placed into midfield for mapping purposes given the crowded rear; his recent form (2/8f/STA best) and headgear switch to a p (hood) at this trip is interesting, but six runs without a win and limited Standard AW exposure (2W from sim-going perspective) make him reliant on pace collapse rather than outright ability.

runners_data.name: Orange Emperor
runners_data.note: A hold-up specialist who has been run from behind throughout his career and is mapped to midfield only because of field composition; James Fanshawe is an active 6/19 trainer in 14 days, but Orange Emperor's Standard AW record is one placing from ten comparable runs and his 7f form (one second at Goodwood) has yet to translate on this surface.

runners_data.name: Superstorm
runners_data.note: The bottom-rated runner (OR 52) has won over 7f at Goodwood and showed a recent second on that course, but needs a visor (headgear flagged) and has been out only 9 days; he is a true hold-up type pushed into midfield on the map by field shape, with Mikkel Mortensen riding — an apprentice combination that makes aggressive late positioning a strategic challenge in an already congested rearward group.

races.paceDynamic: Bundok is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine rivals disputing the lead, he is poised to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop around Kempton's flat polytrack over seven furlongs. Standard-to-Slow conditions will encourage a measured early tempo, rewarding horses who can travel comfortably just off the pace rather than those forced to make up significant ground late. Musical Soldier is the standout prominent racer who can slot in directly behind Bundok and enjoy the clearest run, while Something Coming represents the best-credentialed hold-up type if the pace proves genuinely honest. The field holds more true hold-up types than can realistically race from the rear — Viviana, Chapman's Peak, Orange Emperor, and Superstorm are all natural hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map, meaning they will be competing for the same ground in behind Bundok and Musical Soldier, with Musical Soldier likeliest to secure the prime tactical position. This race shape — a lone leader setting a controlled tempo — strongly favours a prominent, well-positioned racer who can track the pace and kick from just off it; hold-up horses will face a congested passage and may find the tempo insufficient to generate a winning late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Musical Soldier Controls Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Bundok sets a fair but not fierce gallop and Musical Soldier travels smoothly in second throughout.
scenarios.body: Musical Soldier's recent run of form (three wins in his last six, OR 61, 138lbs but tactically versatile) sees him dictate from a prominent position, launching a sustained challenge turning for home that Bundok cannot repel over the extra furlong of seven furlongs. The controlled tempo suits a horse that wins when covered up in mid-race before being produced with a clean challenge, and his trainer Ollie Sangster's sharp 3/30 in 14 days confirms yard confidence.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Bundok Gallops To Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Bundok is allowed a completely uncontested lead and the apprentice jockey Alfie Redman perfectly manages the fractions on standard-to-slow ground.
scenarios.body: Bundok settles into his own rhythm unchallenged at the front, the pace stays honest but never punishing, and the prominent style that defines his profile proves entirely race-shape compatible despite his style-fit caveat being linked to distance step-up rather than absolute position. Something Coming and Musical Soldier, closest in behind, are best placed to chase but fail to reel in a horse who has been given the perfect lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge Too Late
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo quickens materially early, cramming the hold-up horses who find cleaner air late than expected.
scenarios.body: With several redistributed hold-up types forced into genuine midfield positions — Chapman's Peak, Orange Emperor, Viviana, Superstorm — one may find daylight and finish powerfully if the pace collapses on the inside rail and a gap appears wide. However, given Standard-to-Slow conditions and Bundok's tendency toward a measured gallop, this shape requires near-perfect luck in running and timing from jockeys of limited experience.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Draw Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the field fans wide early, riders lose position, and the race devolves into a scramble for limited racing room in the straight.
scenarios.body: Apprentice jockeys dominating this field — Redman, Lewis, Swallow, Carmichael, Moore, Murphy — increase the risk of positional errors, and if pace judgement breaks down entirely the race falls to whichever horse stumbles into the cleanest run regardless of planned role. Something Coming and Superstorm, both with scope to stay on, could benefit from late disorder if early positional battles cause traffic problems for the principals.

watchPoints.text: Musical Soldier ran yesterday (1-day return) — if Libby Swallow reports any stiffness or the horse is not fully recovered, his chance evaporates entirely; watch the pre-race show and market move closely.

Bundok has not raced in 82 days and steps up to 7f having finished 11th at that trip last time — if he comes off the bridle early and fails to sustain his lead, the entire pace architecture collapses and the race loses its defining tactical shape.

Four genuine hold-up types (Viviana, Chapman's Peak, Orange Emperor, Superstorm) plus Something Coming will all be seeking similar ground in the back half of the field — watch for a traffic pile-up on the home turn as inexperienced apprentices struggle to find racing room simultaneously.

Standard-to-Slow conditions are slower than the declared Standard going — horses who have poor form on slower surfaces, particularly Viviana (1 placing from 7 Standard AW runs) and Bundok (1 from 4 sim-going), face a compounded ground concern.

Trainer Ollie Sangster has saddled three runners in 14 days from 30 (10% strike rate) but Musical Soldier is clearly the stable flagbearer in current form; any unexpected market drift for Musical Soldier given the 1-day return should be treated as significant negative intelligence.

races.name: Unibet More Extra Place Races Maiden Stakes (gbb Race)
Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day/ebf Novice Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Al Widyan
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding runner with a respectable form figure of 4 on Good; a natural hold-up horse who will be mapped into midfield here as the rear is congested, meaning he races somewhat out of role — his chance depends on threading through rather than sweeping from the back.

runners_data.name: Asgar
runners_data.note: Clive Cox juveniles often improve sharply second time out after a 87-day break; prominently raced and likely to press Stormy Winter, making him the main pace rival and a genuine each-way threat if the leader ties up.

runners_data.name: Blue Victory
runners_data.note: William Knight's hold-up 2yo posted a fifth on Good at Goodwood and will need the front rank to set a genuinely taxing gallop before she can make meaningful ground from the rear on this flat track.

runners_data.name: Coatimundi
runners_data.note: Tagged as fading in the finish from a Charles Hills yard with modest 14-day figures; the hold-up style combined with a tendency to weaken late makes this a difficult profile on a track where you need sustained finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Farasan
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden runner stepping back to 6f having been tried over 7f on Good; Oisin Murphy adds class in the saddle, and if the pace proves strong enough, the shorter trip may sharpen his finish from a hold-up berth.

runners_data.name: I Am Royal
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with an unknown style profile; Billy Loughnane has been in good form and a 9-day turnaround suggests connections are confident — the third-place finish on Good over 6f gives him a legitimate form peg to hang his hat on.

runners_data.name: Stormy Winter
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner in the race; Cieren Fallon is an accomplished pace judge and Saeed bin Suroor's operation runs horses fit, with 19 days between runs — a controlled solo lead on Standard to Slow is precisely the scenario that plays to this profile.

runners_data.name: Agent Rose
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams runner returning after 84 days with just one outing on Standard going in similar conditions that produced no win or place; a true hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield position on the map, meaning she races out of her natural role and the chance must be tempered accordingly.

runners_data.name: Love Always
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster debutante carrying a 7lb claiming allowance for Libby Swallow; no form to assess and going preference is unknown — complete unknown quantity that adds noise to any analytical framework.

runners_data.name: Sierra Belle
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's consistent 2yo has back-to-back second-place finishes on Good over 6f, giving her the clearest recent form reference in the field; prominent style means she will be in the mix early and is the chief rival to Stormy Winter from a positional standpoint.

runners_data.name: Snow On The Beach
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with headgear noted; modest record on Fibresand and Standard going with no wins or places in similar conditions, and the apprentice claim for Mason Paetel may not compensate for the limited profile.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Progress
runners_data.note: Daisy Hitchins' yard is 0/3 in the 14-day window and this horse has back-to-back double-figure finishes on Standard and Good going; the fade-in-finish flag compounds an already unappealing record, making this a very difficult case to make.

races.paceDynamic: Stormy Winter is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to push her off the front, she will control tempo from the gates through the Kempton 6f on what the going report confirms is Standard to Slow — a surface that rewards economical front-end gallopers who don't burn fuel needlessly. Asgar, Sierra Belle, and Snow On The Beach will press from prominent positions just behind, providing a structured gallop rather than a chaotic burn-up, and that suits a horse who can dictate her own rhythm. The hold-up horses — Al Widyan, Blue Victory, Farasan, Coatimundi, Agent Rose — will be chasing from midfield or deeper, and on a flat, right-handed polytrack loop where sustained galloping matters more than a late sprint, closing ground from well off the pace is a statistical disadvantage. This race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-lead profile: a controlled but honest tempo set by one horse, with closers having to run through traffic on a track that rarely rewards deep hold-up tactics over 6f. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Al Widyan and Agent Rose are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield positions, but Stormy Winter and the genuine prominent types — Asgar and Sierra Belle — are most likely to actually secure their natural early positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stormy Winter Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Stormy Winter leads unchallenged and sets a fair but unspectacular tempo that keeps the closers flat-footed.
scenarios.body: Stormy Winter dictates from the front, the Standard to Slow surface blunting the ability of hold-up horses to reel her in, and she has enough in reserve to repel any prominent challenger in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Asgar or Sierra Belle press Stormy Winter into a strong pace and the leader ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The increased tempo drains Stormy Winter's advantage and one of the pressing trio — Asgar, Sierra Belle, or Snow On The Beach — sustains better to the line in a race run at a proper clip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong early and a prominent-mapped horse finds clear daylight in the straight.
scenarios.body: Al Widyan or I Am Royal, racing closer to the pace than their natural style, finds a gap as the front two tire and picks up the pieces — though this requires the redistribution to work in their favour.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closer Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unusually strong for a novice 6f and the entire front rank exhausts itself within the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A genuine hold-up horse like Farasan or Blue Victory sweeps past a tiring field, though this is the least likely shape given Standard to Slow going blunts closing surges and the pace is not expected to be truly scorching.

watchPoints.text: Stormy Winter has a clean lead with no rival to push her — if Cieren Fallon finds an uncontested rhythm through the first two furlongs, the race may be decided before the straight is reached.

Asgar returns after 87 days for Clive Cox, a trainer who typically has horses ready to improve sharply on a second outing; watch the market move on him pre-race as this could be a sharper performance than his debut suggests.

Al Widyan and Agent Rose are both genuine hold-up horses mapped into midfield due to field congestion — if neither can get back to their natural position, expect their chances to be compromised regardless of how the pace develops.

The Standard to Slow going report for this 6f contest is confirmed; closers relying on a final-furlong burst should be treated with caution as the surface consistently blunts late runs on the Kempton AW straight.

Love Always is a complete unknown on debut for Ollie Sangster with no going or distance form to assess — any significant market support for this runner should be flagged as stable information not visible in the data.

races.name: Unibet/ebf Novice Stakes (gbb/gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Anchor
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Clare Hobson whose best form reads 0 in recent starts; sim-going record of 0 wins from 2 on similar surface, and 28 days between runs is fine, but the fading finishing pattern and 12f trip history suggest a lack of the late spark needed when pace is likely to be moderate.|

runners_data.name: Fortitudine
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's three-year-old won on debut over 11f on Standard AW and boasts a perfect sim-going record of 1W from 1 run; William Buick's positioning intelligence is key here — tracking the leader from a prominent pitch is precisely his natural role and this trip extension looks manageable.|

runners_data.name: No Ordinary Joe
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old veteran who is flagged as fading in the finish and whose most recent run was a poor ninth; hold-up style is undermined by a genuine tendency to not see out races, and the sim-going record of just 1 win from 15 attempts tells its own story.|

runners_data.name: Shadow Road
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over 11f on Standard AW and has the tactical advantage of dictating this contest; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) is noted — this horse is racing slightly out of role in terms of field dynamics — but as the sole genuine pace-setter it is best placed to secure its natural position rather than be displaced.|

runners_data.name: Brave Hunter
runners_data.note: Won twice over 12f on Good ground and handles the trip, but the visor headgear, 55 days off, and a form string of -62725 raise fitness and consistency questions; a genuine front-runner by nature, the redistribution to midfield reflects that Shadow Road and Fortitudine are likely to beat it to the prominent berth, meaning it may race uncomfortably against type.|

runners_data.name: Roxy Power
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's three-year-old is completely unknown — no going profile, no days-since-last-run data, no recent form — making her an impossible quantity to map with confidence; Silvestre De Sousa's experience is a positive but the lightly-raced flag and unknown style (U) mean she could surface anywhere in the field.|

races.paceDynamic: Shadow Road is the confirmed front-runner and, with just one other naturally prominent horse (Fortitudine) to press from the outside, is likely to control this 1m3f trip at a measured, sustainable gallop on a Standard to Slow Kempton AW surface. Fortitudine under William Buick will sit close to the pace from stall position, potentially applying gentle pressure but unlikely to force Shadow Road into a genuinely searching tempo. Brave Hunter, a true prominent type, has been displaced to a midfield mapping because there are more pace-minded horses than positions at the front — Shadow Road and Fortitudine are best placed to secure that ground, leaving Brave Hunter to race against its nature. This shape — a controlled lead with a single nearest pursuer — strongly favours prominent-to-handy types who can travel close to the pace without being exposed early, rather than deep closers who need a strong gallop to generate the gaps they require.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shadow Road Controls, Fortitudine Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Road sets a comfortable, uncontested tempo and the race develops into a two-horse tactical duel turning for home.
scenarios.body: Shadow Road dictates from the front at a pace that suits those close to the action, with Fortitudine ideally placed to strike under Buick's timing; the slow-to-moderate gallop means ground is never truly softened up for hold-up horses and the winner comes from the front two.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early fractions are truly dawdling and a late sprint is needed, bringing genuine hold-up types into contention.
scenarios.body: A very slow pace could compress the field and gift Anchor or Roxy Power a chance to close late, but both are lightly exposed or form-inconsistent at this trip; the Standard to Slow surface does not particularly assist pure finishers and the lack of a true strong pace makes this shape less reliable to materialise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Brave Hunter Outruns Midfield Tag
scenarios.trigger: If Brave Hunter pushes forward from the gate and reclaims its natural prominent position, disrupting the projected order.
scenarios.body: A brisker early pace would emerge if Brave Hunter forces its way close to Shadow Road, compressing the advantage of the lead horse and potentially suiting a more progressive prominent type; however, the horse races out of its mapped role and its OR of 80 leaves it with ground to find against 120-rated rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Roxy Power — lightly raced and an unknown quantity — proves significantly better than current form suggests.
scenarios.body: Roxy Power's unknown going profile and complete absence of recent form data make her a wildcard; in a race where tactical uncertainty could create a vacuum, a horse with unexposed potential could exploit it, but the lack of any evidence base means this scenario carries minimal weight.

watchPoints.text: Shadow Road and Fortitudine are the two principal pace-setters — watch whether Fortitudine applies pressure from the break or settles behind; the gap between these two in the early stages will define the tempo of the entire race.

Brave Hunter will likely attempt to push forward from the gate despite its midfield mapping — if Billy Loughnane commits early and creates a contested pace, the dynamic shifts significantly and the front-runners become more vulnerable.
Roxy Power's complete absence of form data makes her a genuine unknown — monitor her pre-race market move and paddock behaviour as the only available signals before the off.

No Ordinary Joe's fading-in-finish flag over a 1m3f trip on this surface warrants monitoring — if the pace is genuinely slow, the 10-year-old may appear to travel well before emptying in the closing stages, falsely suggesting a competitive run.

The Standard to Slow going (confirmed across multiple races on the card) adds a small stamina premium — horses whose recent form includes this surface condition, particularly Fortitudine and Shadow Road, hold a subtle edge over those whose form base is on faster ground.

races.name: Try Unibet's New Smartview Racecards Fillies' Handicap Stakes (London Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Zoustar Dreams
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who wants to lead; wears a hood and has won three of six career starts, all at 5f on Good, making the step to 6f on Standard To Slow AW a query — her sim-going record of 0 wins from 2 placed in similar conditions adds caution.

runners_data.name: Got The Booty
runners_data.note: Clive Cox filly returning from 79 days off, which is a notable freshness flag; has placed twice on Standard AW over 6f and is a natural front-runner who will battle Zoustar Dreams for the lead, but her fitness level after a lay-off is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Just Queen High
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a disappointing recent record on Good ground but a sole win came on Heathway AW; Cieren Fallon is an asset and her profile suits a pace-pressured race, though her OR=67 and limited AW form mean confidence is tempered.

runners_data.name: Amelia's Joy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins over this course and distance — the most course-relevant form in the field; wears a hood, is only 16 days since her last run suggesting fitness, and David Probert's booking strengthens the case for a positive run if she finds a clean position.

runners_data.name: Egotistical
runners_data.note: Roger Varian three-year-old who placed three times on Standard AW going and won on Good ground over this trip; Ray Dawson takes the ride for a yard in fine 14-day form (5/16), and she is likely to press for a prominent slot in a competitive pitch.

runners_data.name: Startled Lady
runners_data.note: Won her last Goodwood 6f race on Good ground and has placed twice on Standard AW, so the surface is not a concern; William Knight has placed three from 15 runners in the last fortnight and she is a live each-way contender if she settles off the pace pressure.

runners_data.name: Remi Mae
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is a major jockey booking for Andrew Balding's hold-up filly, whose form figure of 3-3-3 shows remarkable consistency without winning; wears a tongue-tie and her Standard-going placed run fits this surface, making her the most naturally suited horse to the anticipated pace shape.

runners_data.name: Overbudget
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's lightly-weighted three-year-old is a natural front-runner or prominent racer by style; the field's pace density means she cannot access her preferred position, and with a STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 her chance is materially discounted — her AW record shows just one place from eight runs in similar conditions.

races.paceDynamic: Zoustar Dreams and Got The Booty are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this 6f Kempton AW sprint, creating a genuinely competitive early pace rather than a lone breakaway. With Amelia's Joy, Egotistical, and Startled Lady all pressing for prominent positions behind them, this field is pace-rich and the gallop should be honest-to-strong throughout, compressing the race shape and reducing the premium on raw early speed. The Standard To Slow going (confirmed across all races on the card) will add a little extra test to legs late, meaning those who travel smoothly into the race without burning fuel chasing the pace carry a tactical advantage. Overbudget is a natural prominent type pushed to a midfield mapping because there are simply more pace-pressing horses than positions available — she is unlikely to secure her natural slot. This race shape overwhelmingly favours hold-up or late-midfield runners who can settle off a pressured pace and pick up the pieces in the final furlong, with prominent horses drawn into a war for position facing the greater risk.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Zoustar Dreams and Got The Booty burn each other out through a strong early pace, setting up a clear run for hold-up horses in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: The contested lead between the two front-runners creates an honest-to-strong gallop that stretches the field; hold-up types who have settled comfortably will be finishing strongest as the principals tire. Remi Mae and Just Queen High, both genuine hold-up horses with course-relevant form, are ideally suited to sweep past a tiring front rank.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent trio settles just off the contested pace without being sucked into the early war, allowing them to kick at the two-pole.
scenarios.body: Amelia's Joy has the best recent course-and-distance form in this group, with two wins over the trip on Kempton's AW surface, and if David Probert slots her into a controlled prominent pitch she becomes the most dangerous mid-race mover. Egotistical's Standard-going profile also suits here, having placed three times in similar conditions, making her the secondary candidate if she avoids being dragged wide early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Got The Booty or Zoustar Dreams is able to dictate at a controlled tempo and the field fails to close down a handy lead in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Standard To Slow conditions add time but not necessarily a stamina collapse, and if neither front-runner truly pushes the other hard through the first two furlongs, a settled front-runner could hold on. Got The Booty's back-to-form Standard-going placed runs suggest she is the more likely of the two to coast rather than burn, though her 79-day absence is a risk factor.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so strong that the entire field is strung out and an unconsidered runner picks a clean path through late.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability shape but a fully contested pace with multiple prominent horses scrapping for position does occasionally produce a clean late run from an unpredicted angle. Overbudget, though racing out of her natural prominent role and carrying a STYLE_FIT discount, could in theory latch onto the pace fluidly if redistribution goes her way — however, the more likely beneficiary of a chaotic shape remains Remi Mae.

watchPoints.text: Watch Zoustar Dreams and Got The Booty in the opening furlong — if both commit fully to the lead, the pace will be strong enough to compromise both their chances and dramatically lift the hold-up horses' prospects.

Overbudget's redistribution to midfield means Mason Paetel (3) will need to adapt race tactics completely; watch whether she is able to slot in behind the pace rather than chasing it wide, which would further erode her chance.

Got The Booty's 79-day absence makes her fitness an open question — watch her in the paddock and early in the race for any signs of greenness or ring-rustiness that might cause her to drop away before the pace truly begins.

Remi Mae's tongue-tie is noted and her tendency to post placed finishes without winning is a pattern to track — if Oisin Murphy takes her back early to avoid the pace battle, monitor whether she has the finishing kick to convert a prominent hold-up position into a victory.

Standard To Slow going is confirmed across the entire card; any horse that appears to be struggling with the surface early (notably those with only Good-ground form) should be treated with caution in running.

races.name: Unibet Supporting Safer Gambling Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Aigeas
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Oliver Cole, running just 7 days after last start; has a win and a place in six sim-going runs and a rare Kempton AW success at 6f over similar conditions, though the slight step up in trip may test his ability to close effectively in a race where midfield is already crowded.

runners_data.name: Sierra Sands
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's progressive three-year-old returns after 32 days with back-to-back wins at Goodwood, including a 7f success; David Egan takes the ride for a trainer firing at 2/19 over the last fortnight, and his prominent style is perfectly suited to a race where pace is genuine and a position just off the leaders is available.

runners_data.name: Shaman Champion
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan partners this Clive Cox runner who has shown ability at 7f on Standard AW ground with a placed effort in one relevant sim-going run; a modest recent form string including two double-figure finishes at Goodwood suggests he is best when conditions and track suit, and Cox's 3/21 recent strike rate indicates the stable is in decent nick.

runners_data.name: Raggaas
runners_data.note: Simon and Ed Crisford's runner arrives on the back of a Goodwood win and a runner-up at the same venue, both at shorter trips; his one sim-going run produced a placed effort and Jack Mitchell retains the ride — he travels prominently and is unexposed enough that stepping back to 7f on a surface he handles may suit.

runners_data.name: Comic Hero
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's charge — a winner over 7f at Kempton AW and placed at 6f at Goodwood — is a genuine prominent racer by style but the field's pace congestion means he is unlikely to secure that forward berth, leaving Oisin Murphy to manage from a less natural position; his STYLE_FIT of 0.93 reflects that compromise, though Balding's prolific 13/64 14-day return shows the team is thriving.

runners_data.name: Hardy's Hero
runners_data.note: William Haggas's consistent front-runner has finished second in four of his last five starts over 7f and will look to set sail from the front with Cieren Fallon; his problem is Manly Fireball's presence, which means the lead will be contested rather than gifted — if he gets a soft time in front he is dangerous, but a duel is more likely than a solo show.

runners_data.name: Manly Fireball
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane's mount for Richard Hughes has won over 6f on Standard AW and carries significant sim-going experience (8 from 9 runs on similar surfaces), suggesting the track and conditions suit; he will press for the lead alongside Hardy's Hero and his lower weight (129lbs) gives a slight advantage, though his best wins have come at 6f and the 7f trip requires him to maintain his gallop for longer.

runners_data.name: Blakefell
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's runner is a natural prominent racer with placed efforts on Standard AW ground at 7f, but the depth of pace in this field means Silvestre De Sousa is likely to find him pushed into a mid-division role he doesn't naturally fill; last ran just 9 days ago and the trainer has had no winners in 16 attempts over 14 days, so the booking angle is uninspiring even if the horse's course-distance profile is relevant.

races.paceDynamic: Hardy's Hero and Manly Fireball are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this Kempton AW 7f, creating a genuine, honest gallop on a Standard to Slow surface that will stretch the field early. That contested pace is unlikely to be suicidal but it will be consistent enough to test those who chase hard, meaning the race is likely to be run at a tempo that suits horses who can travel efficiently just off the speed rather than deep closers who need a true burn. Sierra Sands, Shaman Champion, and Raggaas are best placed to exploit the prominent-to-midfield berths that genuine pace clears up, and this race shape tilts clearly in favour of the prominent racer who can sit second or third and pounce once the front-running duel begins to tell. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position — Comic Hero and Blakefell are genuine prominent racers who are likely to be squeezed back into midfield roles they are not fully comfortable with, with Hardy's Hero and Manly Fireball most likely to actually own the early lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Hardy's Hero and Manly Fireball fight for the front and sustain an honest gallop, setting it up for a tracking racer to strike.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners press each other through the early and middle stages, ensuring the pace is consistent and the race is run to suit horses travelling just off the speed; Sierra Sands and Raggaas, both in-form prominent types with recent wins, are ideally positioned to pounce as the leaders tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Dictates, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners — most likely Hardy's Hero — gets a soft lead and controls a measured tempo.
scenarios.body: A subdued early gallop allows the leader to coast in front and quicken clear on a surface that suits a relaxed front-runner who conserves energy; Hardy's Hero, trained by Haggas and with a consistent second-place record over 7f at this trip, is the beneficiary if Manly Fireball concedes the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners burn each other out rapidly and a fast-finishing midfield horse arrives late with a sustained run.
scenarios.body: A genuinely strong pace sees the front pair weaken in the final furlong, opening the door for a horse with a clean run from mid-division; Aigeas, a hold-up type with Kempton AW sim-going form, and Comic Hero, a natural prominent racer pushed back into a deeper position, are the logical beneficiaries though Comic Hero's redistribution tempers confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Standard To Slow Upsets Order
scenarios.trigger: If the Standard to Slow surface noticeably tests stamina and reshuffles the running order in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Heavier-than-expected conditions blunt the speed of the front two sooner than anticipated, rewarding those with stamina reserves and proven form on similar surfaces; Blakefell, with multiple 7f runs on Standard AW ground and sim-going placed efforts, and Manly Fireball, who carries positive sim-going data, may cope better than rivals without that profile.

watchPoints.text: Sierra Sands and Raggaas are both on sharp form and ideally placed stylistically — if either secures a clean position just behind the front-running pair, the pace dynamic sets up directly for them and one or both could dominate the market move pre-race.

Hardy's Hero and Manly Fireball will contest the lead — monitor early in-running to see which horse capitulates first, as the loser of that duel is likely to stop abruptly in the final 2f and create traffic for any horse trying to come through on the inside.

Comic Hero and Blakefell are genuine prominent types squeezed into midfield — if either finds a gap and creeps closer than expected on the home turn, the STYLE_FIT discount applies but they become more dangerous than their mapped position suggests.

The going is confirmed Standard to Slow throughout the card — Manly Fireball's sim-going profile (8 from 9) and Aigeas's Kempton AW win on similar give both horses a surface edge that could matter if conditions are more testing than the Standard label implies.

Mason Paetel claims 3lbs for Aigeas, bringing the horse's weight down to an effective low in the race — worth monitoring whether the claim is a live booking or simply a conditional placing, as the combination of light weight and hold-up style could make Aigeas a sleeper if the pace collapses late.

races.name: Bet £20 Get £20 With Unibet Handicap Stakes (London Middle Distance Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Joseph
runners_data.note: Holds a clear course profile on the AW and has won twice in five runs on standard going — the headgear (p) adds a tactical note — but his hold-up style requires genuine pace from Pershalla to have something to aim at, and 16 days since last run is no concern at four years old.

runners_data.name: Madjid
runners_data.note: Back within seven days of a win, which suggests confidence from Harry Charlton, and his two recent victories (1m2f STA, 1m2f GOO) confirm he's in career-best form — he's a hold-up type who needs a strong gallop to peg back a front-runner and the compressed pace here is his chief enemy.

runners_data.name: Pershalla
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and the key pace-setter for the entire field; she races prominently out of her natural hold-up role (STYLE_FIT 0.94), so while she shapes the race, her ability to maintain that lead through the final quarter-mile is the central question, particularly on a surface that has been grinding slower as the evening progresses.

runners_data.name: Extraterrestrial
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford runner returning from 73 days off — fitness is a live question — and while his form figures include placed efforts at this trip, he is a genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield mapping by the congestion of closers; his style discount (0.91) is real and his chance depends on finding cleaner air than the race shape is likely to provide.

runners_data.name: Thatcham
runners_data.note: Limited form — just three runs, all placed fifth or sixth — and his natural hold-up inclination is crowded out by the cluster of rear-runners, placing him in a mapped midfield position that isn't his preference; the Richard Hannon yard is quiet at 0/42 over 14 days and there is little in the form book to suggest he can overcome an unfavourable race shape.

runners_data.name: Rogue Desire
runners_data.note: 90 days off is the standout flag here, and all his recent form has come at 7f, making this step up to 1m3f a significant unknown; Jack Morland sends him out with a prominent tag, and if he can sit second to Pershalla from the gate, he gets the race shape he needs — but course fitness and the trip extension are genuine concerns.

races.paceDynamic: Pershalla is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-horse field and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure her, Cieren Fallon can dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable tempo over this 1m3f trip on a surface playing Standard to Slow. The hold-up brigade — Joseph, Madjid, Extraterrestrial, and Thatcham — all want to come from off the pace, meaning the race is likely to develop into a steady-run procession with a single horse on the engine and a bunch of closers in a compressed group behind. Rogue Desire provides the only other possible prominent interest, but her recent form at shorter trips makes her a minor factor at best in shaping the pace. This race shape heavily favours a horse capable of tracking Pershalla in second or third and kicking on from the two-pole, giving a tactical edge to prominent racers or the most decisive of the hold-up horses who can travel smoothly into the race without cover; note also that the field holds more hold-up types than can realistically fill the rear, meaning Extraterrestrial and Thatcham are most likely to be pushed forward against their preference, with Joseph and Madjid the likelier true backmarkers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pershalla Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Pershalla leads unopposed at a measured gallop and the hold-up pack fails to close the gap off a slow pace.
scenarios.body: Fallon sets a frugal tempo that suits a horse on the pace, and with no rival to test her early, Pershalla gets a dream lead through the first mile before the field strings out in the straight; horses who travel prominently behind her are best placed to pounce as the tempo lifts.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Reels Her In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and one of the true closers times their run perfectly to overhaul Pershalla in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A very slow tempo collapses Pershalla's advantage approaching the home straight, allowing the most progressive hold-up runner to swoopwith a sustained late run on the AW surface; Joseph, wearing headgear and with strong course form, is best-positioned stylistically for this outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Rogue Desire or a redirected hold-up type secures a prominent position and outkicks the field from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: With the pace controlled, a horse able to sit second or third and produce a decisive burst gets a clean passage without being stuck in traffic; Rogue Desire's placed form at 7f suggests a turn-of-foot if she can get into this race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Pershalla sets an unusually slow tempo and multiple closers arrive simultaneously in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: A truly crawling gallop on a Standard to Slow surface condenses the field into a sprint finish from two out, favouring the highest-rated and freshest finisher with no premium on positional racing; Madjid's two recent wins give him the raw form ceiling to benefit from a messy, bunched conclusion.

watchPoints.text: Pershalla leads unopposed — watch whether Cieren Fallon quickens or dawdles through the first half-mile, as the pace she sets determines whether the hold-up pack can close at all.

Extraterrestrial is 73 days off the track and carries a style discount — watch his market movement in the final minutes; if supported, connections may have schooled him to race closer to the pace to compensate.

Joseph wears headgear (p-first time or continuation) — watch his early behaviour and whether David Egan elects to push forward rather than drop in, which could dramatically alter the race map if he challenges Pershalla for the lead.

The going report shows every race this evening at Kempton trending Standard to Slow on the AW — watch whether this surface is tiring late-season, which would penalise hold-up runners needing a strong final-furlong kick more than a front-runner already in full stride.

Madjid runs just seven days after winning — watch for any signs of freshness or bounce effect in the early stages, as a tired closer in a race with a slow pace has very little chance of reeling in Pershalla.
